chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Talha ibn Zayd, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said: I heard my father (peace be upon him) saying:
Indeed, God, Mighty and Majestic, hates every frequent divorcer, the taster.

key_terms.ذَوَّاق: Lit. 'taster'; one who repeatedly samples women through serial marriage and divorce; the intensive form indicates habitual action
key_terms.مِطْلَاق: One who divorces frequently and excessively; the intensive form (fi'al) indicates habitual repetition
key_terms.يُبْغِضُ: Hates/detests; expresses divine displeasure, a stronger concept than mere disapproval

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about a man who divorces his wife frequently?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) narrates from his father Imam al-Baqir (AS) that Allah despises the man who divorces repeatedly and the 'taster' — one who marries women only to sample them and then discard them through divorce. This hadith comes from the chapter on the abhorrence of divorcing a compatible wife and reflects the Shia jurisprudential stance that while divorce is technically permissible, it is among the most detestable of lawful acts when done frivolously. The term 'dhawwaq' (taster) refers to a man who serially marries and divorces women out of desire rather than genuine commitment.
